blocks.help: Adds a value to a collection: at the end of a list or deque, into a set, or into a queue, stack or priority queue.
Removes every item of a collection.
True when a list, deque or set holds the value, or a map has the key.

Runs blocks once for each item of a list, deque, set or text, in order. Read-only items can't be changed; a copy can, without changing the collection; an editable item changes the item in the collection.
Runs blocks once for each key of a map, smallest key first, with the key and its value. Neither can be changed.
True when a collection has no items.
The item at a position of a list or deque (the first is at 0), or the value for a key of a map. A position or key the collection does not have stops the program with an out-of-range error.
How many items a collection has.
A list, deque or set with these items. It takes its type from where it is plugged in, such as the value of a 'create' block whose type is chosen.
The item a queue, stack or priority queue gives next: the oldest of a queue, the newest of a stack, the largest of a priority queue. An empty one stops the program (debug builds report it).
Removes the item at a position of a list or deque (the first is at 0); the items after it move up. A position the list does not have stops the program with an out-of-range error.
Removes the item a queue, stack or priority queue gives next. An empty one stops the program (debug builds report it).
Removes a value from a set, or a key and its value from a map. Nothing happens when it is not there.

Changes the item at a position of a list or deque (the first is at 0), or sets the value for a key of a map, adding the key when the map does not have it yet. A position the list does not have stops the program with an out-of-range error.
Puts the items of a list or deque in order, smallest or largest first. The items must be comparable.
Leaves the innermost loop.
Skips the rest of this round of the innermost loop.

Runs blocks once, then again while a condition is true; choose until in the menu to repeat until it becomes true. The condition sees only what is visible before the block, not the variables its blocks create.

label.friendly: go on into the next case

blocks.help: Put last in a case of a switch: after this case's blocks, the next case's blocks run too, without checking its value.
Counts from one number to another, running blocks for each value.
Repeats blocks forever (use stop or break to leave).
Runs blocks only when a condition is true. Add else if and else parts with ⊕, and remove them with ⊖.
Repeats blocks a number of times.

Runs the blocks of the case whose value equals the value switched on, or the default part when no case does. The value is a whole number, a character or a value of an enum; each case value must be fixed when the program is built, and no two may be the same. Add cases and the default part with ⊕, and remove them with ⊖.
Pauses the program for a number of seconds, which may have a decimal part (0.5 is half a second).
Repeats blocks while a condition is true; choose until in the menu to repeat until it becomes true.
The message of an error that a catch part caught.
Throws the error this catch part caught again, for a try block further out to catch. It can only be used inside a catch part.
Stops the blocks here with an error of this kind and this message. The nearest try block around it that catches the kind runs its catch part next; with none, the program stops.

Runs the blocks after try. If one of them throws an error, the first catch part for that kind of error runs, with the error in its variable; the parts are tried in order, and std::exception catches every kind. Add catch parts with ⊕ and remove them with ⊖.
True when there is a file or folder at the path. A path that is not a full path is looked for in the folder the program runs in.

label.friendly: for each line %LINE in file %PATH %BODY if it can't be opened %FAILED

blocks.help: Reads a text file line by line and runs blocks for each line, without its line break. A path that is not a full path is looked for in the folder the program runs in: the project folder, or its sandbox folder when the run settings choose it or the project is not saved yet. Add the part that runs when the file can't be opened with ⊕; without it, nothing runs when the file can't be opened.

label.friendly: open file %PATH for %MODE as %FILE if it can't be opened %FAILED

blocks.help: Opens a text file to read it line by line, to write it from the start, or to add to its end, and names it for the blocks after this one. A path that is not a full path is looked for in the folder the program runs in. Add the part that runs when the file can't be opened with ⊕. The file closes at the end of the group of blocks this block is in.
Reads the next line of a file opened for reading into a text variable, without its line break. True when there was a line to read, false at the end of the file, so it can be the condition of a loop.
Writes values to a file opened for writing or for adding to its end, as print shows them in the console. Untick new line to go on writing on the same line.
Calls a function and uses its result.
Calls a function.
Defines a function: a named group of blocks you can use again.
Leaves the function, giving back a value if the function returns one.
Asks the user to type something and stores it in a variable.
From here on, prints every decimal number with this many digits after the decimal point, also in join and as text. Whole numbers are not changed.
Shows values in the console.
True or false.
True when the condition is false.
True when all (and) or any (or) of the conditions are true.
One of two values, depending on a condition.
The number without its minus sign.
Adds, subtracts, multiplies or divides two numbers, or gives the remainder.
The number if it is between the two limits, otherwise the nearer limit. The lower limit must not be above the higher one: a debug build stops the program then.
Compares two values.
Converts a number to another number type, e.g. a decimal to a whole number.
A function of a number: rounding, roots, powers of e, logarithms, and the angle functions, whose angles are in radians. The result is a decimal number.

A function of two numbers: the first to the power of the second; the angle, in radians, of the point whose y is the first and whose x is the second; or the long side of a right-angled triangle whose other sides are the two.
The larger or the smaller of two numbers.
A number, such as 42 or 3.14.
A random whole number between the two values, including both.
A random decimal number between the two values.

Checks a condition when the program is built, not when it runs: if it is false, the program doesn't build and the message says why. The condition may use only numbers, characters, true/false values and constants with fixed values.
Ends the program. Exit code 0 means success.

The program starts here. A project has exactly one of these blocks. Tick with arguments to read what the program was started with, as a read-only list of text whose first item is the program's own name.
Includes a header of the C++ standard library, such as <cmath>, in the module's code, wherever the block is. The blocks add the headers they need themselves; this is for a header they don't name.

A value as text, written as print writes it: a decimal number with the decimal places 'show numbers with' chose, true or false for a true/false value. A struct cannot be turned into text in one go; join its fields instead.
The text in lowercase or in uppercase. Only the letters A to Z change; every other character stays as it is.
A single character, such as 'a'.
Whether a text contains another text, starts with it or ends with it.
Joins text and numbers into one piece of text.
The number of characters in a text.
The character at a position of a text, counting from 0. A position outside the text stops the program with an out-of-range error.
A piece of text.
The characters of a text from a position, counting from 0, up to this many of them; fewer when the text ends first. A start past the end of the text stops the program with an out-of-range error.
The text with every place where the first text occurs replaced by the second. An empty first text changes nothing.
A list of the parts of a text between its separators. Two separators in a row give an empty part, and an empty separator gives one part for each character.

The number at the start of a text: 12abc gives 12. A text that does not start with a number throws an invalid argument error, and a number too large for its type throws an out-of-range error; the Errors category has the blocks that catch them.
The text without the spaces and tabs at its start and end.

label.friendly: enum %NAME values … share with other modules %SHARED

blocks.help: Defines an enum: a new type whose values are the names listed here, such as the choices of a menu. Add values with ⊕ and remove them with ⊖.
One value of an enum.
The value of one field of a struct value.
Makes a value of a struct from a value for each of its fields, in the order the struct lists them. An empty part leaves its field empty (0, false or empty text).
Gives one field of a struct variable a new value.

label.friendly: struct %NAME has … comparable %COMPARABLE printable %PRINTABLE share with other modules %SHARED

blocks.help: Defines a struct: a new type whose values hold one value of each of its fields. Add fields with ⊕ and remove them with ⊖; each starts with its default value, or empty (0, false or empty text) without one. Tick comparable to compare and sort its values, and printable to print them.

Adds to a variable (+=); choose down by (-=), times (*=), divided by (/=) or mod (%=) in the menu to subtract, multiply, divide or keep the remainder instead, or add to the end (+=) to add text or a character to the end of a text variable. With advanced blocks shown, the menu also has the bitwise forms (&=, |=, ^=, <<=, >>=) for whole numbers.
Creates a variable. It can be used by the blocks after it in the same place.
Turns a true/false variable to the other value: true becomes false, and false becomes true.
The value of a variable.
Creates a variable, or a constant, that every function of the module can use, wherever the block is. A constant needs a value and never changes.
Gives a variable a new value.
